title.narrative: Output 3.2. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative: In December 2023, the Government of Sierra Leone (GoSL) adopted a sustainable mechanism for feeder road maintenance in rural areas using labour-based intensive technologies as part of the Decentralised Road Management Policy. The measure is a sustainable mechanism for the maintenance of rural roads, integrating Public-Private Community Partnerships (PPCP). The mechanism was developed based on findings from a detailed study and the process led by the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) unit, involved consultations of a broad range of stakeholders including community stakeholders, road users, the Sierra Leone Roads Authority (SLRA), district councils, Road Maintenance Fund Administration (RMFA) and the Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) road contractors. The study report which detailed the sustainable feeder road maintenance model was discussed and validated by ILO’s Tripartite Constituents together with representatives of the aforementioned stakeholders at a meeting held in Freetown in November 2023. It is foreseen that the mechanism will not only provide opportunities for employment but also promote entrepreneurship development as a result of the improved access to markets for the targeted rural areas. Between May and December 2023, the ILO, with funding from the European Union EU), provided technical services to the PPP unit, SLRA, the district councils and RMFA throughout the mechanism development process. In particular, the ILO in collaboration with the PPP unit drafted the terms of reference and engaged the consultant to conduct the study- detailing the sustainable feeder road maintenance model. ILO also provided support in the review of all reports and technical backstopping through out the process. The ILO also collaborated with the PPP unit to mobilise relevant stakeholder for discussions and validation of the draft model.

title.narrative: 3.2.1. Number of Member States with measures for decent work in rural areas
Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
The Government of Sierra Leone (GoSL) in collaboration with its social partners supported value chain actors of cassava, oil palm and vegetables adopted an action plan at sub-national level covering the districts of Port Loko, Bo, Bombali and Kenema in June 2023. The purpose was to promote entrepreneurship, business resilience and small and medium enterprise (SME) development, through innovative and inclusive business models by creating an innovation platform for offering opportunities to rural enterprises. These SMEs received several training, mentorship and coaching services from a pool of Training of Trainers (TOTs) from June – December 2023, which helped to increase their entreprenuerial skills and made them more competitive and productive. In addition, a consultant was hired to draft specific interventions for these SMEs to develop new products such as cassava flour, high grade palm kernnel oil for the cosmetic industry and gari for poultry feed. Value chain financing programme was also introduced to enhance access to financial services for these SMEs, cooperatives organizations and other social and solidarity economy enterprises. This platform would remain actiive until June 2025. The ILO with funding from EU hired the consultant that developed the new value chain products, delivered the TOT trainings, mentorship and coaching services to SMEs. These trainings, coaching and mentorship services were offered to increase the capacity of value chain actors in market systems development, entrepreneurship (SIYB and GET Ahead), coopératives training (Think COOP, My COOP), business coaching and psychosocial support to entrepreneurs. SMEDA, the Local Content Agency, APEX Bank and the Sierra Leone Chamber for Agribusiness Development (SLeCAD) received ILO tools to train enterprises and set up the innovation platform.
The ILO also technically supported SLeCAD by providing funds to conduct a financial services mapping study across Port Loko , Bo, Bombali and Kenema, reviewed the report before it was validated by social partners and adopted for implementation as a value chain financing model.
